items.evidence_note: away means at a great distance from the road.
items.sentence: The cabin is far away from the nearest road.

items.evidence_note: away indicates a location far from the city center.
items.sentence: Her office is away from the city center, so the commute takes longer.

items.evidence_note: Uses beginning in the sense of the start or first part of an event.
items.sentence: At the beginning of the lesson, the teacher explained the basic rule first.

items.evidence_note: Uses beginning to mean the initial stage or starting point.
items.sentence: From the beginning, she wanted to understand the core idea before anything else.

items.evidence_note: Shows location in the middle of two places.
items.sentence: The café is tucked between the library and the post office.

items.evidence_note: Shows distribution among two recipients.
items.sentence: She divided the cookies between her two children.

items.evidence_note: Refers to a 100-year historical period.
items.sentence: The castle was built in the 12th century and still stands on the hill.

items.evidence_note: Uses century as a time span in history.
items.sentence: Historians debated how life changed during the 19th century.

items.evidence_note: chief means the person in charge of the group
items.sentence: The chief approved the budget and told the team to start on Monday.

items.evidence_note: chief refers to the boss or leader making decisions
items.sentence: After the meeting, the chief asked every department head to send a progress report.

items.evidence_note: even means level or tied in score
items.sentence: The two teams finished even after the final round, so they had to play one more match.

items.evidence_note: even means flat and level
items.sentence: Keep the shelves even so the books do not slide off.

items.evidence_note: far describes a large physical distance from the road.
items.sentence: The cabin is far from the nearest road, so we have to walk a long way to reach it.

items.evidence_note: far indicates the office is located at a great distance from downtown.
items.sentence: Her office is far from downtown, which is why she takes the train every morning.

items.evidence_note: Refers to a unit of time before an event.
items.sentence: The meeting starts in one hour, so please be ready.

items.evidence_note: Refers to a duration of sixty minutes.
items.sentence: I waited an hour for the train to arrive.

items.evidence_note: Shows location within an enclosed space.
items.sentence: The keys are inside the drawer.

items.evidence_note: Shows being within a building or enclosed area.
items.sentence: Please wait inside the house until the rain stops.

items.evidence_note: just means only a small amount of time is needed.
items.sentence: I just need a minute to finish this form.

items.evidence_note: just means only one, matching the restrictive sense.
items.sentence: She wanted just one ticket for the concert.

items.evidence_note: light means illumination in the room
items.sentence: The room felt brighter when I opened the curtains and let in more light.

items.evidence_note: light refers to a lamp or source of illumination
items.sentence: Please turn on the light so I can read this page.

items.evidence_note: little describes a small physical object, matching the intended sense.
items.sentence: They bought a little table for the kitchen corner.

items.evidence_note: little clearly means small in size, not amount or age.
items.sentence: She packed her clothes into a little suitcase for the weekend trip.

items.evidence_note: Industrial production of goods.
items.sentence: The factory is making thousands of bottles every hour.

items.evidence_note: Creative production of a film.
items.sentence: The studio is making a new documentary about ocean life.

items.evidence_note: more expresses a greater quantity, matching the intended sense of 'más'.
items.sentence: I need more coffee before the meeting starts.

items.evidence_note: more indicates an increased amount, which corresponds to 'más'.
items.sentence: Please add more sugar to the recipe.

items.evidence_note: Refers to the early part of the day.
items.sentence: We will leave in the morning, before the heat gets too strong.

items.evidence_note: Refers to the next day’s early time period.
items.sentence: She finished the report by morning and sent it to the team.

items.evidence_note: Refers to songs and sound played for entertainment.
items.sentence: The music at the wedding kept everyone dancing late into the night.

items.evidence_note: Refers to the art and study of organized sound.
items.sentence: She studies music theory to understand how melodies and harmony work.

items.evidence_note: national describes something belonging to or representing the whole country.
items.sentence: The museum opened a national exhibit that showcases artifacts from every region of the country.

items.evidence_note: national indicates a countrywide program, not a local one.
items.sentence: She won a national scholarship that is awarded by the government to top students across the country.

items.evidence_note: Shows a practical requirement or necessity.
items.sentence: We need more water before the hike starts.

items.evidence_note: Expresses a condition of necessity or lack.
items.sentence: There is a need for better lighting in the hallway.

items.evidence_note: Indicates the present time or current situation.
items.sentence: I am now working from home, so email is the fastest way to reach me.

items.evidence_note: Describes the current state as of today.
items.sentence: The company now has offices in three countries and is hiring again.

items.evidence_note: Uses official to mean authorized or formally issued.
items.sentence: The official report confirmed the new safety rules.

items.evidence_note: Uses official to mean formally approved or public.
items.sentence: She waited for the official announcement before sharing the news.

items.evidence_note: Restrictive sense: the action is limited to one thing.
items.sentence: She only wanted a glass of water, not a full meal.

items.evidence_note: Restrictive sense: the amount of time is limited.
items.sentence: I only have ten minutes before the meeting starts.

items.evidence_note: Active sense of understanding written text.
items.sentence: I like to read before bed to relax.

items.evidence_note: Active sense of processing written material.
items.sentence: She will read the article and summarize it for the team.

items.evidence_note: room means available space for an additional object.
items.sentence: There is enough room for one more chair by the window.

items.evidence_note: room means free space that can be cleared or used.
items.sentence: Please make room on the shelf for the new books.

items.evidence_note: section refers to an internal department handling a business function.
items.sentence: Please send the invoice to the accounting section for approval.

items.evidence_note: section refers to a workplace department responsible for a specific service.
items.sentence: The HR section will handle your benefits questions this afternoon.

items.evidence_note: small describes physical size, matching the intended sense of pequeño.
items.sentence: She bought a small table for the apartment entrance.

items.evidence_note: small refers to a compact object size, clearly the size sense.
items.sentence: The child held a small red ball in both hands.

items.evidence_note: space means physical room or gap between objects.
items.sentence: Please leave a little space between the chairs so people can walk through.

items.evidence_note: space means available room inside a container.
items.sentence: The box is too small, so there is no space for the extra book.

items.evidence_note: stand means a booth or stall set up for selling goods.
items.sentence: The vendor set up a stand at the market to sell fresh fruit.

items.evidence_note: stand refers to a staffed kiosk or booth.
items.sentence: We stopped at the information stand to pick up a map and ask for directions.

items.evidence_note: start refers to the beginning of something.
items.sentence: At the start of the book, the author explains the rules clearly.

items.evidence_note: start marks the opening point in time.
items.sentence: We met at the start of the meeting to review the agenda.

items.evidence_note: Asking for the clock time of departure.
items.sentence: What time does the train leave tomorrow morning?

items.evidence_note: Refers to a specific clock time for scheduling.
items.sentence: Please tell me the time so I can join the meeting on time.

items.evidence_note: work means to do a job or labor
items.sentence: I have to work late tonight to finish the report.

items.evidence_note: work means to be employed and perform duties
items.sentence: She works at the hospital and starts at 7 a.m.

items.evidence_note: access means an entrance or way in
items.sentence: Please use the side access to enter the stadium after your ticket is checked.

items.evidence_note: access refers to an entry point
items.sentence: The museum opened a new access for visitors near the main square.

items.evidence_note: ask means to inquire directly about information.
items.sentence: I will ask the teacher what the homework is.

items.evidence_note: ask means to question someone for a specific answer.
items.sentence: Please ask her where the meeting starts.

items.evidence_note: Physical damage to an object; active sense matches 'romper'.
items.sentence: Please don't break the glass vase when you move it.

items.evidence_note: Causing a mechanism to fail or be damaged; active sense matches 'romper'.
items.sentence: If you twist the handle too hard, you might break the door lock.

items.evidence_note: Refers to a personal motor vehicle.
items.sentence: She parked her car in the garage before dinner.

items.evidence_note: Refers to a road-going automobile.
items.sentence: The car needs new tires before the road trip.

items.evidence_note: Describes limited width or tight spacing.
items.sentence: The alley was so close that two people could not pass side by side.

items.evidence_note: Uses close to mean narrow or tight.
items.sentence: We had to squeeze through a close gap between the fence and the wall.

items.evidence_note: court refers to an open inner patio used for dining and gathering.
items.sentence: We ate lunch in the court behind the old inn, where the tables were shaded by vines.

items.evidence_note: court refers to an enclosed outdoor patio area attached to the building.
items.sentence: The apartment opens onto a quiet court with potted plants and a fountain in the center.

items.evidence_note: Hot tea in a drinking vessel indicates the intended sense is a mug-like cup.
items.sentence: She poured hot tea into a cup before sitting down to read.

items.evidence_note: A kitchen item used for drinking makes the cup sense clear.
items.sentence: He washed the cup after breakfast and put it back in the cabinet.

items.evidence_note: Means to make the amount twice as much.
items.sentence: Please double the recipe so we have enough soup for everyone.

items.evidence_note: Means to increase to twice the current size.
items.sentence: The company will double its storage capacity by adding a second warehouse.

items.evidence_note: Time duration uses eight in the sense of Spanish ocho.
items.sentence: Please set the timer for eight minutes so the pasta does not overcook.

items.evidence_note: Clock time uses eight in the sense of Spanish ocho.
items.sentence: She arrived at eight o'clock and the meeting started right away.

items.evidence_note: exactly marks precise agreement with the intended point.
items.sentence: That is exactly what I meant when I said the plan needed more time.

items.evidence_note: exactly expresses precise timing, matching the intended sense.
items.sentence: She arrived exactly when the meeting was about to start.

items.evidence_note: Physical face on a person, the intended body-part sense.
items.sentence: She wiped the rain from her face before stepping inside.

items.evidence_note: Refers to a person's face as an anatomical feature.
items.sentence: The doctor examined his face for signs of swelling after the fall.

items.evidence_note: ice refers to frozen water used for cooling drinks.
items.sentence: Please add ice to the cooler so the drinks stay cold.

items.evidence_note: ice refers to frozen water on the ground.
items.sentence: The sidewalk was covered with ice after the overnight freeze.
